# brig agent build

Rebuild an agent's image, copy it into a VM and point its template at it

## Synopsis

```text
brig agent build [VM] NAME [--tag TAG] [--no-pull]
```

## Description

Build the image of the agent that agents/NAME/agent.yaml in one of the VM's
config directories describes, with Podman on the host: podman build --pull
-t IMAGE:TAG. TAG is today's date, with -2, -3 and so on if that tag exists
already; --tag sets it. --no-pull keeps the base image as it is.

It then copies the image into the VM, unless the VM has this exact image
already, and makes the template that agent.yaml names use it, in the
workspace of -w. OpenShell can only create and delete templates, so brig
deletes and creates it again. That is safe: a sandbox copies its template
when it is created, so existing sandboxes keep their image. Move them when
it suits you.

Without VM, the one that [`brig use`](brig-use.md) selected is used.

## Examples

```sh
brig agent build dev claude
brig agent build dev pi --tag 2026-10-13-test --no-pull
```

## Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--no-pull` | do not pull the base image first |
| `--tag string` | the image tag (default: today's date) |
| `-w, --workspace string` | the workspace of the gateway to work in (default: $BRIG\_WORKSPACE, else default) |

The [global options](brig.md#options) of brig apply too.
